       N4: Operation Weser (north & south)                                                                                        German player
      April, 1940. The Kriegsmarine is ordered to facilitate the occupation of Norway. In the face of superior enemy assets,
      its surface fleet must risk ferrying the Wehrmacht to multiple ports along the coast. Surprise is crucial, and speed is
      essential.
      Objective
      Two Convoys and one DD Squadron must perform Completion actions in Bergen, Trondheim, and Narvik. All ships
      must ultimately perform Completion actions in Wilhelmshaven or Kiel. Do not allow German ships to be damaged or
      sunk.

CMY                 Operation Weser was successful. As the Wehrmacht launches its attack on Belgium, the Netherlands, and France,
                    Britain is in a state of shock. Chamberlain is no longer Prime Minister and there are calls for Winston Churchill to
 K
        15 +        replace him, but it was Churchill’s ineptitude that led to the fall of Norway. A bitter and frantic political battle ensues
                    in Parliament. Meanwhile, the French government urges its ally to send reinforcements across the Channel.

                    Operation Weser was successful. If there is a British air base in Norway, reduce this outcome one row (to “The Battle
                    for Norway us undecided”). If a Convoy or DD Squadron completed in either Bergen or Trondheim, the Germans now
      11-14         command the skies over Norway. German troops may not have secured every critical port, but it is only a matter of
                    time. If a German BC was damaged or sunk, the Kriegsmarine will be unable to launch aggressive new operations for
                    some time.

                    The Battle for Norway is undecided. If German Convoys and the DD Squadron completed in Norway, the Germans
                    have the upper hand. The invasion of France and the Low Countries may be delayed, in order to allow the Luftwaffe
       6-10         to continue to support the battle in Scandinavia. If only two Convoys completed, Trondheim has proven to be a
                    tough stronghold, but its fate is clear. If a German Convoy did not complete in Narvik, the British may be able to hold
                    out but only if there is a British air base there.
                    What went wrong? If more German ships are damaged or sunk than British ships, Admiral Raeder’s job may be in
                    jeopardy. If both German Convoys failed to complete in Norway, Raeder is replaced. If a British Convoy completed in
         0-5        Narvik or Trondheim, the invasion of France is delayed. If three or more German ships are damaged or sunk, AND only
                    one Convoy or DD Squadron completed in Norway, the invasion of France is called off until German forces on the
                    ground are rescued by airlift.

                    Disaster! If one Convoy and the DD Squadron completed successfully in Norway, the battle may still be won. If the
          -1        British do not have an air base in Norway AND more British ships were damaged or sunk than German ships, AND
        or less     neither German BC was sunk, Norway eventually falls to the Germans. Admiral Raeder is soon cashiered, however,
                    and the invasion of France is postponed until July or August, or until the spring of 1941.
notes: Scenario solitario: si conta un solo punteggio, quello del giocatore, e lo si legge nella Tabella dell'Esito.
Le rotte stampate come lunghezza in segmenti non sono convertite in esagoni: vanno disegnate dal giocatore o calibrate separatamente.
